narrativeProgression.description: Moira outlines the Scottish Green Party’s stance on social and economic issues.
Moira acknowledges a possible preconceived notion about the Green Party’s focus solely on the environment.
She highlights their commitment to social justice issues like poverty, justice, and equality, advocating for a £10 minimum wage by 2020.
She discusses their opposition to policies like Universal Credit and benefit sanctions, as well as the need to tackle tax evasion and avoidance.

narrativeProgression.description: Moira discusses the dangers of TTIP and highlights the mistreatment of asylum seekers in Glasgow, while also advocating for democratic reforms.
Moira raises awareness about TTIP, explaining its potential negative impact on the NHS and workers' rights.
She emphasizes the Scottish Green Party's opposition to TTIP and then shifts focus to the plight of asylum seekers, particularly the “Glasgow Girls”.
Moira advocates for a more democratic system with an elected second chamber, increased representation of women in parliament, and more power to local councils.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: My name is Moira Crawford. I'm the Scottish Green Party candidate for Glasgow North West.
You may have a view of the Scottish Green Party as a party that was a strong concern for the environment.
We do, and I have. But we also care about other things equally strongly.
We care about poverty, justice, equality. And that's why we want to raise the minimum wage.
We want to raise it to a living wage of £10 per hour. Do it in stages so that we get there by 2020.
I'd like to raise some money too. So we'd levy attacks of 2% on the richest 1% of our citizens.
Things we'd like to be a stop to as well. Like to be a stop to the universal credit, to the bedroom tax, to work fair, to the whole benefit sanctions.
And how about the tax evasion and avoidance? We should be stopping that too.
Do you know that the Green Party, the Greens in Europe, are the only party in the EEC who want to stop T-Tip?
T-Tip is the transatlantic trade and investment partnership.
T-Tip would hand over control of our valued services to multinational corporations. We cannot let that happen.
I'm standing for Glasgow North West. That's the constituency of the Glasgow girls.
Those remarkable school girls who took on the system and won on behalf of asylum seekers.
I want to put an end to the shabby treatment of asylum seekers. Let's stop them having to go to Liverpool for their final appeal.
That's destitute asylum seekers, having to travel to Liverpool.
I want to stop them being left in limbo and then gavill detention centre. Some of them for years at a time. We must stop that.
I said earlier, Greens are interested in a better democracy.
So we want an elected second chamber. Let's get rid of the House of Laws. We want women in parliament.
And we want to bring democracy closer to the people. So we want more power to local councils, to local communities.
Let's make a living next night.
This election, I'm standing for what I believe in. I'm voting for what I believe in. I hope you will too.
